The deal implies an equity value of about $1.79 billion when combined with Miro’s net cash, the companies said. Certain Miro shareholders have also agreed to invest $295 million of their proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons

The transaction, which was unanimously approved by the boards of both companies, remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. Until closing, the companies will continue to operate independently.
Miro has around $600 million in annual recurring revenue, with nearly 90% coming from business and enterprise customers, Bending Spoons
CEO and co-founder Luca Ferrari said. Miro is used by more than 250,000 organizations and has nearly 4 million paying users, according to the release.
Miro CEO and co-founder Andrey Khusid said the partnership would allow the company to pursue its vision for an AI-first workspace.
